look_here_first: FOLLOW THE SMALL HAIRY SHOOT TO ITS FLOWERING HEADS. E. ophthalmica (Florida hammock sandmat) typically makes a LOW PROSTRATE hairy colony with small opposite, slightly unequal, finely toothed leaves. At the END of each main shoot or SHORT LEAFY side shoot, many tiny cyathia crowd into a round HEAD (glomerule). E. hirta also has terminal heads but additionally makes AXILLARY heads, often on extended LEAFLESS stalks: seeing just one terminal head does not prove ophthalmica. E. hypericifolia also forms dense heads but generally has SMOOTH STEMS and smooth capsules; E. nutans makes looser leafy clusters and larger leaves. FNA describes ophthalmica's minute capsule as finely APPRESSED-HAIRY, its stipules as narrow and sometimes divided, and its four-angled seeds with a few FAINT CROSSWISE wrinkles. Our existing images SUPPORT head placement, leaf/stem hairs and mat habit, but NOT clear capsule hairs, tiny stipules or seed sculpture. No Hays County native-range finding should be inferred from these mostly nonlocal source photos.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. Opposite leaves, milky latex, cyathia (tiny reproductive structures), 3-lobed dry fruit.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Usually prostrate, rarely ascending, annual (occasionally short-lived perennial) from taproot; slender shoots 6–22 cm. A low spreading habit is suggestive, never sufficient alone.

key_traits.label: Stems
key_traits.text: Fine short appressed hairs (strigillose) mixed with longer spreading hairs (hirsute), often both on the same plant.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite; ovate to oblong, 4–13 × 3–7 mm, asymmetric base, coarse fine teeth (coarsely serrulate), usually with 3 veins emerging near base; center may carry red blotch but many leaves do not.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Distinct, narrow subulate-filiform scales, entire or divided into 2–4 slender triangular/threadlike segments, 0.9–1.5 mm, hairy; lacking dark round glands at base. A magnified true node is needed to distinguish from ordinary hairs.

key_traits.label: Flowering cluster
key_traits.text: Dense CAPITATE terminal glomerules; at ends of main stems or very short leafy side shoots. Small reduced bractlike leaves occur beneath them. Unlike E. hirta, not separate axillary flower heads on long leafless stalks.

key_traits.label: Cyathia
key_traits.text: Tiny involucres about 0.5–0.7 × 0.4–0.6 mm with fine hairs; four yellow-green to pinkish glands, with thin white/pink rims or very small appendages, sometimes without obvious appendages.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Ovoid three-lobed capsule 1–1.2 × 1–1.3 mm, strigillose (finely appressed-hairy), not smooth/glabrous.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Orange-brown to pinkish, narrowly ovoid, sharply four-angled; 0.7–0.9(–1.1) × about 0.5 mm; usually shallow wrinkling and 3–6 faint transverse ridges, occasionally smooth-looking.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: prostrate hairy stems terminating in dense round cyathium heads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flower heads at stem and short LEAFY side-branch tips, not long leafless stalks

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small opposite asymmetric 4–13 mm leaves with coarsely serrulate margins

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: both short-appressed and longer spreading stem hairs
